A U.S.-Iran peace agreement — including the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz — has catalyzed a sharp risk-on rotation across global markets. Bitcoin reclaimed the $65,700 level on June 15, 2026, gaining approximately 2% over 24 hours as the Crypto Fear & Greed Index climbed from the extreme fear zone (20) toward neutral. Spot BTC ETF outflows, which dominated the past five sessions, have flipped to modest net inflows, signaling a pause in institutional de-risking. The SEC's approval of T. Rowe Price's actively managed multi-asset crypto ETF — holding both BTC and ETH — marks a structural milestone in institutional product access.

Market attention pivots to the June 16–17 FOMC meeting, the first chaired by Kevin Warsh. With U.S. inflation at 4.2% in May and CME FedWatch pricing a 97.4% probability of no change, the policy statement's tone is the primary macro variable. The U.S. dollar has held a bullish bias under higher-for-longer expectations, maintaining a historically tight inverse correlation with Bitcoin. Any hawkish Warsh signal would strengthen the DXY further, amplifying headwinds for BTC and compressing crypto market cap from its current $2.24 trillion level.
